newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber eyes INRO, trade sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber eyes INRO, trade sidelined.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market kept a wary eye on the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) after its rubber indicator price fell to levels where it may intervene in the market, dealers said.
"Everybody's waiting for INRO's move. People are sidelined for now," a dealer said.
The five-day indicator ended at 182.48 Malaysia/Singapore cents a kg on Thursday, below the 183.00 cent level where INRO 'may-buy' rubber to support prices in the market.
Most of the trade in Singapore believes INRO will not immediately step in and may wait for the price to fall further.
"I think they'll wait for it to go below 180.00 cents before coming in," one dealer said.
"I think they'll only come in at the must-buy level of 172.00 cents," another trader added.
The market was untraded in the morning session as dealers also waited for leads going into the afternoon session.
"Everybody is sidelined. It's wait-and-see," a dealer said.
At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated steady at 91.50 U.S. cents a kg. September RSS1 was indicated unchanged at 135.25 Singapore cents (94 U.S. cents) a kg.
